findings.title: FEAT-006 is unfinished and the tree is dirty
findings.detail: git status shows uncommitted progress notes in FEAT-006.json. Item 30 is incomplete: ossctl discover, contribution import and targets verify are missing, ossctl up does not report the real resumed count, and item 30's TRACEABILITY rows are not updated. Item 31 has not started: no tests/e2e, upstream_fixture, kiro-cli stub, ossbot-runner.service with full hardening, services.sh/kill list/lib.sh entries or crash-safety runner case. Item 32 has not started: no redeploy, sandbox-llm image rebuild with the new agents, prompts and entrypoints, versions.lock digests, live checks (catalog, doctor --probes, kiro smoke, targets verify, global switch), VERIFICATION 'Phase 2 live checks', FEAT status or findings. Acceptance criteria 1 (e2e part), 2, 3, 5 (test_e2e_proposal) and 6 cannot be checked.

findings.title: A sandbox interruption or restart fails the item instead of re-queueing it
findings.detail: sandboxd records drain-timeout and crash-recovered jobs as state failed, error_class interrupted. runner/stages/common.py job() and runner/llm.py Kiro._once raise StageFailed for every non-succeeded job, so Scheduler.run_one calls fail() and the item becomes FAILED, with the stage run recorded as failed. A sandboxd SIGKILL or restart makes Sandbox.run raise SbxError 503 sandboxd_unreachable, which run_one also routes to fail(). This contradicts AC 32 and the CR-001 runner rule (interrupted job -> stage_run interrupted -> re-queue, max 3). No test covers it. Fix: map error_class interrupted and SbxError 503 to Interrupted (not fail()) and add unit tests.

findings.title: M11 first start is incomplete and the probe-gate 423 turns into a hot loop
findings.detail: Scheduler.first_start only reads probes_status. Nothing calls Sandbox.probes_run with resolved models, although M11 and test_e2e_first_start require it. A failed catalog job only logs: there is no catalog_empty alert and no hourly retry, and dispatch continues, so items go FAILED with model_unavailable instead of waiting. While sandboxd answers 423 safety_probe_missing (always after the item-32 image rebuild, because agent_configs_sha256 is in the probe key), every Kiro-stage item re-runs each 10 s tick. Each run costs about 5 GitHub GETs, a stage_runs row recorded failed internal:SbxError and 2 audit events, with no backoff, and it is not counted toward REQUEUE_MAX. Three items exceed the 5000/h read-token limit. Fix: complete M11 (catalog -> probes_run -> stages), hold Kiro stages before any transition or stage run until the catalog and probes are ready, send catalog_empty with an hourly retry, and back off on 423.

findings.title: A drain interrupts running stages at the next heartbeat
findings.detail: Gate.check (require_running + require_up) runs at every StageRun.tick (every 2 s inside Sandbox.run), so draining or down cancels the running sandbox job within seconds. DESIGN 13.5 says the lifecycle only stops new work and running work finishes (sandboxd drain gives running jobs S s; AC 31 counts 'N finished'). test_heartbeat_interrupts_a_running_stage[draining] asserts the wrong behaviour. The build-plan wording conflicts with DESIGN, and DESIGN wins. Fix: at heartbeat check kill and pause only; check the lifecycle before a stage and before each new job; treat sandboxd's 423 draining or interrupted result as Interrupted.

findings.title: The scout snapshot is a fetch job in the task volume, before gate 1
findings.detail: scout.py runs a fetch-profile, fetch-entrypoint job (repo_mode rw, ossbot-task-<cid>, depth 1, prefetch false) before Start work. DESIGN 9.1 row 2a and 9.5a specify a fetch-free shallow snapshot by the runner's read path into a snapshot job, 9.1 says fetch and the task volume come only after Start work, and AC 37 says no fetch job runs before Start work. No repo code runs, but the fetch egress and a task volume are used pre-gate-1, and the decision is recorded only in the FEAT findings, not in DESIGN, an ADR addendum or TRACEABILITY. Fix: implement the read-path snapshot, or ask (hard rule 12) and record the decision change, with AC 37 and test_e2e_proposal worded to match.

findings.title: Hitting proposal.max_per_day re-runs the whole scout every tick
findings.detail: The daily cap is checked only when POST /proposal arrives (429). scout.run turns that into Deferred and the item stays SCOUTING, which Scheduler._eligible always dispatches. The next tick clones again and runs another full Kiro scout session, until the 24 h window rolls. This is reachable with the defaults (proposals_per_cycle 3 every 6 h against max_per_day 5). Fix: pre-check the cap before scouting, or hold the item until the window opens.

findings.title: The tests-required backstop trusts the scout's claim that the repo has no suite
findings.detail: review.run sets has_suite = bool(proposal.tests). A scout answer of tests: [] with any no_suite_reason disables the deterministic missing-tests rejection (tests_exception no_suite), so the AC 41 and user rule depends on untrusted model output. Fix: detect a suite deterministically from the fetched tree (test_globs or known test configs, recorded in fetch.json), and refuse or flag proposals whose no_suite_reason contradicts it.

findings.title: Expired and snoozed proposals are re-scouted without checking that they still apply
findings.detail: AC 37 and 9.5b say an expired proposal is re-scouted only if it is still relevant, and the state machine has PROPOSAL_EXPIRED -> SKIPPED. scout.run moves PROPOSAL_EXPIRED and PROPOSAL_SNOOZED straight to SCOUTING without re-reading the issue (closed, assigned, linked open PR, rediscover rules), and no code takes the SKIPPED edge. Fix: run a cheap relevance check before re-scouting, skip with a reason when it fails, and add tests.

findings.title: The claim wait never ends for an item without an issue
findings.detail: With proposal.claim_comment on, the PROPOSAL_APPROVED -> FETCHING guard requires an issue_claim. fetch._claim raises Deferred('claim_without_issue') every tick for repo or PR /work items, with no message to the owner. Exempt items with no issue in the guard, or notify the owner once.
